title: Input-Length Counting Run
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean word and let $d$ be a one-work-tape configuration on input $x$, in phase count and with its input head at position $1$. Suppose the work tape is blank at offsets from the work-head position in the range $-1$ through the number of binary digits of the length of $x$. For every natural number $n\le |x|$, there is a time $t$ such that $t+2c(n)=5n$, where $c(n)$ is the number of ones in the binary expansion of $n$, and after $t$ steps the machine is in phase count with the input head at position $n+1$, the work tape containing the binary expansion of $n$ over a segment of its length, and the work head at its original position. At every time $u\le t$, the work-head position lies between one cell left of its initial position and its initial position plus the number of binary digits of $n$.
hypotheses_covered: work tape blank at offsets $-1$ through the binary length of $|x|$
